records.label: spacr.qt.sound#3
records.source: **Nothing exists while sound is off.** The master switch defaults to off, and until somebody turns it on :func:`apply_sound_preferences` returns before constructing anything: no thread, no event filter, no Qt Multimedia import. An application-wide event filter costs every event in the process (measured at 0.93 us per event per filter), so the filter is installed only while a click or hover sound is actually wanted, and removed the moment neither is.
records.context: **Nothing exists while sound is off.** The master switch defaults to off, and until somebody turns it on :func:`apply_sound_preferences` returns before constructing anything: no independent execution path, no event filter, no Qt Multimedia import. records.translation: **No existe nada mientras el sonido está desactivado.** El interruptor general está desactivado de forma predeterminada, y hasta que alguien lo activa :func:`apply_sound_preferences` retorna antes de construir nada: ningún hilo, ningún filtro de eventos, ninguna importación de Qt Multimedia. Un filtro de eventos para toda la aplicación tiene un coste en cada evento del proceso (medido en 0.93 us por evento y por filtro), así que el filtro solo se instala mientras se quiere realmente un sonido de clic o de paso del cursor, y se retira en cuanto no se quiere ninguno.

records.label: spacr.qt.sound#4
records.source: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the GUI thread.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is paid ONCE, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and logged rather than felt. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the GUI thread against the real stack.
records.context: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the main GUI execution path.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is paid ONCE, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and logged rather than felt. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the main GUI execution path against the real stack.
records.translation: **Qt Multimedia solo se toca en el hilo de la GUI.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` es propietario de ``QMediaDevices`` y de cada ``QSoundEffect`` y vive donde vive el bucle de eventos de la aplicación; el ``QThread`` dedicado se queda con la parte realmente lenta, que es sintetizar un conjunto de sonidos (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy y escrituras de archivos, nada de Qt Multimedia). Conectarse al servidor de sonido es lento -- 354 ms medidos en una estación de trabajo con PipeWire --, así que se paga UNA VEZ, en un temporizador inactivo después de activar el sonido (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), y se registra en lugar de notarse. Reproducir un sonido ya cargado es ``play()``, que retorna de inmediato: 0.007-0.014 ms en el hilo de la GUI con la pila real.

Reopening Preferences with sound on then segfaults, or wedges the interface with an empty Preferences frame until it is force quit.
